newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian Moslem leader for force against Israelis.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian Moslem leader for force against Israelis.

text.p: The Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar, one of the Sunni Moslem world's highest authorities, said force was the right response to Israeli practices in Jerusalem.
"We must confront Israeli arrogance and encroachments on Jerusalem by force...with stones and with bullets," he told a seminar in Cairo on Monday evening.

At the same meeting, the Egyptian minister in charge of Islamic affairs had proposed that Moslems and Christians visit Jerusalem in vast numbers to assert their claim to religious sites in the holy city.

But the spiritual leader of the Egyptian Coptic Church, Pope Shenouda III, strongly disagreed with the minister, saying that Arabs should boycott Israel in every way and that force was the only language that Jews understand.

The three men were speaking at a seminar organised by the Egyptian union of journalists on the clashes which broke out between Israeli troops and Palestinians after Israel opened a tunnel near the Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem.
The Sheikh of al-Azhar, Mohamed Sayyed Tantawi, said all revealed religions approved the use of force in self-defence and in defence of religious sites.
"We must not our enemy and the enemy of our holy sites in Jerusalem feel comfortable or stable. They must feel we are still alive and there is still blood in our veins," he added.

Mahmoud Hamdi Zakzouk, the minister of Awqaf (Moslem religious endowments), said: "If Moslems and Christians flocked to visit Jerusalem, in their hundreds of thousands a year, perhaps the situation would now be different.
"The world and the Israelis would know that the hearts and feelings of Moslems and Christians are attached to Jerusalem."
"It would put constant pressure on Israeli intransigence and make them feel that that these holy places have people who will cling to them until they are liberated," he added.
Zakzouk's proposal appeared to be purely personal. The Egyptian government has neither prevented nor encouraged Egyptians who try to visit Jerusalem on pilgrimage.

Pope Shenouda, who has excommunicated Copts who visit Jerusalem and then refuse to repent, said he continued to oppose Christian pilgrimage to Jerusalem as long as Israel controlled the Arab eastern sector of the city.
"The boycott upsets the Israelis. They welcome visits to the Moslem and Moslem holy sites because it's in their interest. It makes tourism and the Zionist economy flourish," he said.

"They also brainwash visitors from the Arab world. All the simple Egyptian Copts who have visited Israel come back with a good impression of life in Israel, of Israelis and their progress in every sphere of life," he said.
"But visiting the Christian holy places takes only four days, not enough to judge life in Israel," he added.
The pope, who has a following of at least six million people in Egypt and the Egyptian diaspora, said he had little hope from peace talks with Israel unless the Arabs were stronger.

"Negotiations don't lead to any results. Even if they reach a fragile result like the Oslo agreement, the Israelis renege on it later. To be quite frank the only thing that works with the Jews is force," he said.
"Without force, Israel will not be frightened of us, or take us into account, or respect its agreements with us.
"For us to defeat the Jews, we must have strength and effective weaponry. Otherwise the Jews will continue to trample on the dignity of the Arabs," he added.
